headline: Qualcomm reportedly mulls Tenstorrent takeover for $8B-$10B, eyeing AI chipmaker
summary: The deal, if it proceeds, would be one of Qualcomm's most expensive acquisitions and values Tenstorrent at a significant premium, according to The Information.
details: Qualcomm is reportedly evaluating an acquisition of Jim Keller-led AI processor developer Tenstorrent. The potential transaction could value the company at between $8 billion and $10 billion, making it one of Qualcomm's most expensive deals if it proceeds.
The Information reports that discussions are ongoing, but there's no guarantee of a deal. Qualcomm is particularly interested in Tenstorrent's RISC-V-based AI accelerators and data center CPU IP.

Qualcomm already has its own AI accelerators (AI200/AI250) and is developing server CPUs, including a recent acquisition of Ventana Micro for RISC-V CPU design. The potential Tenstorrent acquisition would add another layer to its multi-faceted strategy.

The high valuation is notable, as Tenstorrent was reportedly seeking $800 million at a $3.2 billion valuation last year. It's unclear if the current $8-10 billion valuation is performance milestones-based.

Experts suggest the acquisition might be more about talent and future architecture than just hardware. Tenstorrent has a strong team of engineers from companies like AMD, Apple, Intel, and Tesla, led by industry veteran Jim Keller.
Qualcomm has a history of acquiring elite engineering teams, like Nuvia, to accelerate its roadmap. This deal could secure significant RISC-V expertise and a highly skilled chip development team.

headline_marked: [[Microsoft launches Surface Laptop & Pro]] with Snapdragon X2 chips, up to $600 price hike
headline: Microsoft launches Surface Laptop & Pro with Snapdragon X2 chips, up to $600 price hike
summary: Microsoft's latest Surface Laptop and Pro now feature Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 chips, boasting 53% faster graphics. However, starting prices have jumped by up to $600, with reduced base storage.
details: Microsoft has officially launched updated versions of its Surface Laptop (8th generation) and Surface Pro (12th generation). Both devices are now powered by the latest Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 chips, with starting prices for both set at $1,499.

The new Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 chips promise significant performance improvements, offering up to 53% faster graphics performance compared to the previous generation. Users can also expect extended battery life, with Microsoft claiming up to 15.5 hours.

The new Surface Laptop starts at $1,599, marking a substantial $600 increase from its previous $999 starting price. Additionally, the base storage configuration has been halved to 256GB, a reduction from the prior generation's 512GB base.

Similarly, the Surface Pro's new starting price is $1,499, up from its previous $999. It also reverts to a 256GB base storage configuration, and notably, this price does not include the essential detachable keyboard.

These significant price increases are not unique to Microsoft, reflecting a broader trend in the PC industry. Component supply shortages continue to impact the cost of RAM and storage, leading to inflated prices across new Windows laptops featuring the latest silicon.

Beyond the internal upgrades, the new Surface devices introduce fresh color options. The 13.8-inch Surface Laptop is now available in a new greenish "Jade" color, while the Surface Pro offers a goldish "Dune" option. Both models are available for purchase starting today.

These releases follow Microsoft's earlier announcement of the Surface Laptop Ultra, a higher-end device expected later this year. The Ultra will feature Nvidia RTX Spark chips and is positioned as Microsoft's direct competitor to the MacBook Pro.
